data.title: Extract review and evaluation sub-agents into dedicated plugin agents

content.text: ## Context

This epic was originally about extracting all review and evaluation sub-agents (red team, blue team, feasibility reviewer, completion verifier) from inline generic dispatches into dedicated named plugin agents with their own `agents/*.md` files. The majority of that scope — red-team-reviewer, blue-team-filter, feasibility-reviewer, and completion-verifier — was absorbed and delivered by epic bbba-8154 (Planning Resilience). Those four agents now exist as named files under `plugins/dso/agents/` and are dispatched with fallback patterns in preplanning and brainstorm.

What remains is a second tier of generic dispatches: skills that use `subagent_type: "general-purpose"` with a prompt loaded inline or from a prompt file, without a corresponding named agent persona file in `plugins/dso/agents/`. These roles are consistent enough across the codebase to benefit from dedicated agent definitions — clearer persona ownership, easier per-role tuning, and a single source of truth for the prompt.
## Remaining work
Sub-agents currently dispatched as generic that should be extracted into dedicated plugin agents:

- **SC Coverage evaluator (haiku/sonnet/opus tiers)** — sprint's 3-tier success-criteria coverage gate dispatches three separate `general-purpose` sub-agents (haiku fast-path, sonnet mid-tier, opus arbiter) using prompts from `skills/sprint/prompts/sc-coverage-haiku.md`, `sc-coverage-sonnet.md`, and `sc-coverage-opus.md`. Each tier has a distinct role and output contract and would benefit from a named `dso:sc-coverage-haiku`, `dso:sc-coverage-sonnet`, and `dso:sc-coverage-arbiter` (or a single `dso:sc-coverage-evaluator` with tier passed as input). Found in: `plugins/dso/skills/sprint/SKILL.md:354,413,471`.

- **Scenario Red Team / Blue Team in epic-scrutiny-pipeline** — the brainstorm scrutiny pipeline dispatches a `general-purpose` sonnet sub-agent for failure-scenario generation (red team) and a second for scenario filtering (blue team), using inline-loaded prompt files from the caller's `prompts/` dir. Unlike the preplanning phase-e dispatch (which already references `dso:red-team-reviewer` / `dso:blue-team-filter`), the scrutiny pipeline does NOT reference the named agents — it dispatches raw `general-purpose` with scenario-specific red-team and blue-team prompt files. Found in: `plugins/dso/skills/shared/workflows/epic-scrutiny-pipeline.md:246,248`.

- **Web research sub-agent in epic-scrutiny-pipeline** — Step 2 of the scrutiny pipeline dispatches a `general-purpose` sonnet sub-agent for web research (WebSearch/WebFetch aggregation). This role is distinct from the feasibility reviewer and is currently entirely inline. Found in: `plugins/dso/skills/shared/workflows/epic-scrutiny-pipeline.md:187`.

- **Gap classification sub-agent in sprint remediation loop** — Phase H of sprint dispatches a `general-purpose` sonnet sub-agent to classify each failing success criterion as `intent_gap` vs `implementation_gap` before routing to remediation tasks. The prompt lives in `skills/sprint/prompts/gap-classification.md` and the logic is stable enough to warrant a dedicated `dso:gap-classifier` agent. Found in: `plugins/dso/skills/sprint/prompts/remediation-loop.md:23`.

- **Oscillation-check sub-agent in sprint remediation loop** — Phase H also dispatches a `general-purpose` sonnet sub-agent to run `/dso:oscillation-check` inline before creating remediation tasks. Found in: `plugins/dso/skills/sprint/prompts/remediation-loop.md:8`.

- **validate-work sub-agents (local-validation, ci-status, issue-health, staging-check, staging-env-test)** — all five validate-work sub-agents use `general-purpose` with no named agent. Sub-agents 1–3 are haiku-tier mechanical runners; Sub-agents 4–5 are sonnet-tier with conditional branching logic. Could be extracted as `dso:validator-local`, `dso:validator-ci`, `dso:validator-issue-health`, `dso:validator-staging-deploy`, and `dso:validator-staging-env`. Found in: `plugins/dso/skills/validate-work/SKILL.md:149,164,177,189,248`.

- **debug-everything sub-agents (triage, safeguard-analysis, critic-review, merge-verify, gha-scanner)** — multiple phases of debug-everything use `general-purpose` with inline-loaded prompt files: Phase C triage (sonnet), Phase D safeguard analysis (opus), Step 5 critic review (sonnet), Phase L merge-verify (sonnet), and the GHA scanner sub-agent (haiku). Found in: `plugins/dso/skills/debug-everything/SKILL.md:458,496,705,942` and `plugins/dso/skills/debug-everything/prompts/gha-dispatch.md:31`.

- **retro skill reviewers** — the retro skill dispatches five reviewers as `general-purpose` using reviewer prompt files from `docs/reviewers/`. These roles are well-defined and could each become named agents. Found in: `plugins/dso/skills/retro/docs/review-criteria.md:37`.

- **doc-writer dispatch** — `update-docs` and sprint doc-story dispatch both read `agents/doc-writer.md` inline and use `subagent_type: "general-purpose"` because `dso:doc-writer` is not a registered `subagent_type`. The agent file already exists; the remaining work is to update dispatch instructions to use a first-class named `subagent_type` if the Claude Code Agent tool ever supports plugin-registered types, OR to treat the current pattern as the canonical form and document it as intentional. Found in: `plugins/dso/skills/update-docs/SKILL.md:67`, `plugins/dso/skills/sprint/SKILL.md:1350`.
## Success Criteria

- For each role above, either a dedicated plugin agent file exists at `plugins/dso/agents/dso:<agent-name>.md` (for roles without one), or the dispatch site is explicitly annotated as "intentional general-purpose" with a rationale comment.
- Dispatch sites reference the named agent by file and reduce inline prompt content to thin wrappers.
- Retro reviewers each have a named agent file in `plugins/dso/agents/`.

- The scrutiny pipeline scenario red/blue team dispatches reference `dso:red-team-reviewer` / `dso:blue-team-filter` (already named in preplanning) rather than loading separate scenario-specific prompt files as raw general-purpose agents.
## Out of Scope
- Fallback patterns (`general-purpose` as a fallback when a named agent type is unregistered) — these are intentional degradation paths, not extraction targets.
- One-off open-ended research dispatches that are genuinely ad hoc (e.g., the orchestrator directly running WebSearch before handing off to a sub-agent).
- Error-retry escalation paths that re-dispatch as `general-purpose` on named-agent failure — these are recovery mechanisms, not primary dispatch patterns.
## Notes

- Previous scope absorbed by bbba-8154: red-team-reviewer, blue-team-filter, feasibility-reviewer, and completion-verifier were extracted as named plugin agents under `plugins/dso/agents/` and integrated into preplanning (phase-e) and brainstorm with named-agent dispatch + general-purpose fallback.
- Description rewritten 2026-05-11 during /dso:prioritize-epics Phase 4 cleanup based on codebase audit.
